title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 5. The Story of the Setubandha Lake
html:
Through a sleepless night the Lord yearns for Krishna; Krishnadasa tells Him the extent of Mathura-mandala and the story of the Setubandha Lake, where Krishna, calling Himself Rama, built a dam of stones and trees in a contest with Radha; hearing this secret, the Lord dances in Radha's mood

Verse 1

ततः सुप्तोऽपि भगवान् भक्तिरससमन्वितः।
उत्कण्ठितः कृष्णलीलां गायन् प्रेमाश्रु मोचयन्॥१॥

tataḥ supto'pi bhagavān bhaktirasasamanvitaḥ|
utkaṇṭhitaḥ kṛṣṇalīlāṁ gāyan premāśru mocayan||1||

tatah — then; suptah — lying down to sleep; api — though; bhagavan — the Lord; bhakti-rasa-samanvitah — filled with the rasa of devotion; utkanthitah — full of longing; krishna-lilam — the pastimes of Krishna; gayan — singing; prema-ashru — tears of love; mochayan — shedding.

1Then the Lord, though He had lain down to rest, was filled with the rasa of devotion: full of longing, He sang of Krishna's pastimes and shed tears of love.

Verse 2

प्रतिक्षणं पृष्टवान् स कृष्णदास वदस्व मे।
शर्वरी दीर्घतां प्राप्ता मम दुःखप्रदायिनी॥२॥

pratikṣaṇaṁ pṛṣṭavān sa kṛṣṇadāsa vadasva me|
śarvarī dīrghatāṁ prāptā mama duḥkhapradāyinī||2||

prati-kshanam — every moment; prishtavan — asked; sah — He; krishnadasa — O Krishnadasa; vadasva — speak; me — to Me; sharvari — the night; dirghatam — length; prapta — has reached; mama — to Me; duhkha-pradayini — causing pain.

2Every moment He asked, "Krishnadasa, talk to Me! This night has grown so long — it torments Me."

Verse 3

स प्राह शृणु हे नाथ मथुरामण्डलस्य च।
प्रमाणं कथ्यते विज्ञैश्चतुरशीतिक्रोशकम्॥३॥

sa prāha śṛṇu he nātha mathurāmaṇḍalasya ca|
pramāṇaṁ kathyate vijñaiścaturaśītikrośakam||3||

sah — he; praha — said; shrinu — hear; he natha — O Lord; mathura-mandalasya — of Mathura-mandala; cha — and; pramanam — the extent; kathyate — is declared; vijnaih — by the learned; chatuh-ashiti-kroshakam — of eighty-four kroshas.

3He answered, "Listen, O Lord. The learned say that Mathura-mandala extends for eighty-four kroshas1.

Verse 4

क्रमतो दर्शयिष्यामि स्थिरचित्तो भवान् यदि।
भविष्यसि ततो मह्यं सुखं स्याद्भक्तवत्सल॥४॥

kramato darśayiṣyāmi sthiracitto bhavān yadi|
bhaviṣyasi tato mahyaṁ sukhaṁ syādbhaktavatsala||4||

kramatah — in order; darshayishyami — I shall show; sthira-chittah — steady-minded; bhavan — You; yadi — if; bhavishyasi — will be; tatah — then; mahyam — to me; sukham — happiness; syat — will be; bhakta-vatsala — O You who love Your devotees.

4I shall show You all of it in order, if You will keep Your mind steady; then I too shall be happy, O You who love Your devotees.

Verse 5

आगत्य कुण्डोत्तरतः कियद्दूरे सरोवरम्।
सेतुबन्धाख्यकं पश्य श्रीकृष्णेन च निर्मितम्॥५॥

āgatya kuṇḍottarataḥ kiyaddūre sarovaram|
setubandhākhyakaṁ paśya śrīkṛṣṇena ca nirmitam||5||

agatya — going; kunda-uttaratah — north of the pond; kiyat-dure — a little way off; sarovaram — the lake; setubandha-akhyakam — called Setubandha; pashya — behold; shri-krishnena — by Sri Krishna; cha — indeed; nirmitam — made.

5Going a little way north of the pond, behold the lake called Setubandha — Sri Krishna Himself made it."

Verse 6

श्रुत्वा सविस्मयं प्राह पुलकाञ्चितविग्रहः।
अस्य विवरणं ब्रूहि कृष्णदासेति सादरम्॥६॥

śrutvā savismayaṁ prāha pulakāñcitavigrahaḥ|
asya vivaraṇaṁ brūhi kṛṣṇadāseti sādaram||6||

shrutva — hearing; sa-vismayam — in wonder; praha — said; pulaka-anchita-vigrahah — His body thrilled with gooseflesh; asya — of this; vivaranam — the account; bruhi — tell; krishnadasa — O Krishnadasa; iti — thus; sa-adaram — respectfully.

6Hearing this, the Lord, His whole body thrilling, said in wonder and with respect, "Tell Me all about it, Krishnadasa."

Verse 7

इति श्रीगौरचन्द्रस्य वचनं श्रवणामृतम्।
पिबन् कृष्णमनुस्मृत्य प्राह प्रहसिताननः॥७॥

iti śrīgauracandrasya vacanaṁ śravaṇāmṛtam|
piban kṛṣṇamanusmṛtya prāha prahasitānanaḥ||7||

iti — thus; shri-gaurachandrasya — of Sri Gaurachandra; vachanam — the words; shravana-amritam — nectar for the ears; piban — drinking; krishnam — Krishna; anusmritya — remembering; praha — said; prahasita-ananah — with a smiling face.

7Thus drinking the words of Sri Gaurachandra, nectar to the ears, and remembering Krishna, he began with a smile:

Verse 8

एकदा रसिकशेखरो हरि-
र्गोपिकारसविनोदविनोदी।
सरसि चात्र नवकुञ्जरतुल्यः
क्रीडति रघुवरोऽहमिति जल्पन्॥८॥

ekadā rasikaśekharo hari-
rgopikārasavinodavinodī|
sarasi cātra navakuñjaratulyaḥ
krīḍati raghuvaro'hamiti jalpan||8||

ekada — once; rasika-shekharah — the crown of rasikas; harih — Hari; gopika-rasa-vinoda-vinodi — who delights in the sports of rasa with the gopis; sarasi — in the lake; cha — and; atra — here; nava-kunjara-tulyah — like a young elephant; kridati — was sporting; raghu-varah — the best of the Raghus; aham — I am; iti — thus; jalpan — prattling.

8"Once Hari, the crown of rasikas, who delights in the sports of rasa with the gopis, was frolicking in this lake like a young elephant and chattering, 'I am the best of the Raghus!'2

Verse 9

प्राह तं रमणीशिरोमणिराधा
गोपपुत्रस्त्वमसि गोधनचारी।
सत्यधर्मप्रतिपालकराज-
स्तस्य कर्म परदुर्घटमेव॥९॥

prāha taṁ ramaṇīśiromaṇirādhā
gopaputrastvamasi godhanacārī|
satyadharmapratipālakarāja-
stasya karma paradurghaṭameva||9||

praha — said; tam — to Him; ramani-shiromani-radha — Radha, the crest-jewel of beautiful women; gopa-putrah — a cowherd's son; tvam — you; asi — are; godhana-chari — a grazer of cattle; satya-dharma-pratipalaka-rajah — the king, protector of truth and dharma; tasya — his; karma — deed; para-durghatam — impossible for others; eva — indeed.

9Radha, the crest-jewel of lovely women, said to Him, 'You are a cowherd's son who grazes the cattle. That king was the guardian of truth and dharma — His deeds are beyond anyone else.

Verse 10

सिन्धुबन्धनरावणनाशन-
मेतदेव हि तस्य सुशोभनम्।
मा कुरु निजगुणप्रकाशनं
बालिकावसनभूषणचौर॥१०॥

sindhubandhanarāvaṇanāśana-
metadeva hi tasya suśobhanam|
mā kuru nijaguṇaprakāśanaṁ
bālikāvasanabhūṣaṇacaura||10||

sindhu-bandhana-ravana-nashanam — bridging the ocean and destroying Ravana; etat — this; eva — alone; hi — indeed; tasya — to him; su-shobhanam — befitting; ma kuru — do not make; nija-guna-prakashanam — a display of your own virtues; balika-vasana-bhushana-chaura — O thief of young girls' clothes and ornaments.

10To bridge the ocean and slay Ravana — that befits Him alone. Don't go parading Your own virtues, You thief of young girls' clothes and ornaments!'3

Verse 11

कृष्ण आह परमकौतुकराशि-
र्हास्यकौतुकरसैकविलासी।
सर्वसद्गुणनिधिरहमेव
जानीहीति त्वमसि गोपकुमारी॥११॥

kṛṣṇa āha paramakautukarāśi-
rhāsyakautukarasaikavilāsī|
sarvasadguṇanidhirahameva
jānīhīti tvamasi gopakumārī||11||

krishnah — Krishna; aha — said; parama-kautuka-rashih — a treasury of the greatest fun; hasya-kautuka-rasa-eka-vilasi — whose one delight is the rasa of laughter and pranks; sarva-sat-guna-nidhih — the treasure-house of all good qualities; aham — I; eva — alone; janihi — know; iti — this; tvam — you; asi — are; gopa-kumari — a cowherd girl.

11Krishna, a treasury of fun whose one delight is the rasa of laughter and pranks, replied, 'I alone am the treasure-house of every virtue — know that, for you are only a cowherd girl.

Verse 12

सर्वपर्वतमहाधनबाणैः
प्रस्तरा यदि कदापि न भेद्याः।
तर्हि सर्वगुणरत्नसमेतं
पश्यत भावनिधेऽपि प्रभावम्॥१२॥

sarvaparvatamahādhanabāṇaiḥ
prastarā yadi kadāpi na bhedyāḥ|
tarhi sarvaguṇaratnasametaṁ
paśyata bhāvanidhe'pi prabhāvam||12||

sarva-parvata-maha-dhana-banaih — by all the mountains, great riches (?) and arrows; prastarah — stones; yadi — if; kada api — ever; na bhedyah — cannot be split; tarhi — then; sarva-guna-ratna-sametam — endowed with all the jewels of virtue; pashyata — behold (you all); bhava-nidhe — O treasure of feeling; api — indeed; prabhavam — the power.

12Though stones can never be split, not by all the mountains, nor by great riches and arrows4, still behold, O treasure of feeling, the power of one who possesses every jewel of virtue!'

Verse 13

श्रुत्वा सर्वाः परमरसिकाराधिकावाक्यसारं
बद्ध्वा वृन्दं परमरभसात् प्रस्तरादीन् स्वसख्यः।
आनिन्युस्ताः सतरुनिचयांस्तेन बद्धं कृतं तत्
पश्यन्त्यस्ताः सजयध्वनिभिस्तं प्रणम्याशशंसुः॥१३॥

śrutvā sarvāḥ paramarasikārādhikāvākyasāraṁ
baddhvā vṛndaṁ paramarabhasāt prastarādīn svasakhyaḥ|
āninyustāḥ satarunicayāṁstena baddhaṁ kṛtaṁ tat
paśyantyastāḥ sajayadhvanibhistaṁ praṇamyāśaśaṁsuḥ||13||

shrutva — hearing; sarvah — all; parama-rasika-radhika-vakya-saram — the gist of the words of Radhika, supreme among rasikas; baddhva — forming; vrindam — a band; parama-rabhasat — with great eagerness; prastara-adin — stones and the like; sva-sakhyah — her friends; aninyuh — brought; tah — they; sa-taru-nichayan — together with heaps of trees; tena — by Him; baddham — bridged; kritam — was made; tat — that; pashyantyah — watching; tah — they; sa-jaya-dhvani-bhih — with cries of "Victory!"; tam — to Him; pranamya — bowing; ashashamsuh — praised.

13Hearing the gist of the words of Radhika, supreme among rasikas, all her friends gathered in a band and eagerly brought stones and the like together with heaps of trees, and with them He built the dam. Watching it, they bowed to Him with cries of 'Victory!' and sang His praise.

Verse 14

श्रीराधाकृष्णलीला परममधुरहास्यरसादिप्रयुक्ता
[…] गोपिकाभिर्जयति च परमं सन्ततप्रेमपूर्णा।
यां […] श्रुत्वापि परमरसिकास्तौ स्मरेयुः सुखेन
ज्ञानानन्दं हसन्तः सरभसमखिलं मोक्षमप्याक्षिपन्ति॥१४॥

śrīrādhākṛṣṇalīlā paramamadhurahāsyarasādiprayuktā
[…] gopikābhirjayati ca paramaṁ santatapremapūrṇā|
yāṁ […] śrutvāpi paramarasikāstau smareyuḥ sukhena
jñānānandaṁ hasantaḥ sarabhasamakhilaṁ mokṣamapyākṣipanti||14||

shri-radha-krishna-lila — the pastimes of Sri Radha and Krishna; parama-madhura-hasya-rasa-adi-prayukta — imbued with the sweetest rasa of laughter and the rest; […]; gopikabhih — with the gopis; jayati — glory; cha — and; paramam — supreme; santata-prema-purna — full of unceasing love; yam — of which; […]; shrutva — hearing; api — even; parama-rasikah — the supreme rasikas; tau — those Two; smareyuh — would remember; sukhena — joyfully; jnana-anandam — the bliss of knowledge; hasantah — laughing at; sa-rabhasam — eagerly; akhilam — entire; moksham — liberation; api — even; akshipanti — cast away.

14Glory to the pastimes of Sri Radha and Krishna with the gopis5, rich in the sweetest rasa of laughter and the other rasas, ever full of love! Hearing of them, the supreme rasikas joyfully remember those Two; laughing at the bliss of knowledge, they eagerly cast away even liberation entire."

Verse 15

एतद्गौरहरिः कृष्णरहस्यं परमाद्भुतम्।
श्रुत्वा राधारसावेशो ननर्त विवशं मुदा॥१५॥

etadgaurahariḥ kṛṣṇarahasyaṁ paramādbhutam|
śrutvā rādhārasāveśo nanarta vivaśaṁ mudā||15||

etat — this; gaurahari — Gaurahari; krishna-rahasyam — secret of Krishna; parama-adbhutam — most wonderful; shrutva — hearing; radha-rasa-aveshah — possessed by the rasa of Radha; nanarta — danced; vivasham — helplessly; muda — with joy.

15Hearing this most wonderful secret of Krishna, Gaurahari, possessed by the rasa of Radha, danced in helpless joy.

Thus ends the fifth sarga, "The Story of the Setubandha Lake" (Setubandha-sarovara-prasanga), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Krosha: a measure of distance, about three kilometres; eighty-four kroshas is the traditional circuit of Vraja-mandala.
  2. The best of the Raghus: Rama, who built the bridge to Lanka (Setubandha means "the building of the bridge").
  3. An allusion to the stealing of the gopis' garments (Bhagavata Purana 10.22).
  4. The sense of this half of the verse is obscure in the text; the rendering is conjectural.
  5. The printed text of this verse has two gaps (at the beginning of its second and third lines); the translation follows the surviving words.
